topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic origins and clonal evolution of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and enable susceptible cells to evolve into cancers within permissive microenvironments.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how far cancer risk can be attributed to environmental exposures rather than unavoidable chance or inherited predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the causal argument in detail.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce potentially mutagenic DNA damage whose effects depend on cellular metabolism and repair.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require subsequent tumour-promoting conditions before cancer develops.

topics.label: Tissue and life-stage susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why carcinogenic effects depend on the biological context of the exposed tissue and consolidate that principle within the preceding account of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Evidence and methods for assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic exposures can be identified and tested, and why the resulting evidence requires cautious interpretation.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarising its central lessons and framing everyday exposure decisions as risk–benefit judgements.
